Vandals Deface Our Lady Statues, Set Fire to Altar at Medjugorje Shrine The parish called on the faithful to respond 'with prayer, fasting, and forgiveness' as police arrested a suspect and cleanup began days before the Mladifest youth festival. A statue of Our Lady stands in front of St. James Church at the Medjugorje shrine in Bosnia and Herzegovina. (photo: GoneWithTheWind / Shutterstock) EWTN News Staff World July 29, 2026 Vandals desecrated two statues of Our Lady and set fire to the outdoor altar of St. James Church at the Medjugorje shrine in Bosnia and Herzegovina early Tuesday, July 28, days before the shrine’s annual Mladifest youth festival. The statue of Our Lady on Podbrdo, or Apparition Hill, was doused with black paint across the face, chest, and dress, with the words “Devil in a skirt” scrawled on its pedestal, local media reported . The statue of Our Lady at the nearby Blue Cross was similarly defaced, with “EVIL” written on a nearby stone slab. A banner in Polish naming the six alleged seers was left near the Podbrdo statue . Police in Čitluk received the first report at 4:30 a.m. and a report of fire at the recently renovated altar behind St. James parish church at 5 a.m., a police spokeswoman said reportedly. Surveillance footage shows a man dousing the altar with flammable liquid and igniting it. Cantonal police later confirmed to local media that a suspect was arrested Tuesday afternoon. His identity has not been released. ‘Prayer, fasting, and forgiveness’ “We received with great sadness the news of the act of vandalism that damaged the places of prayer in our parish,” the Medjugorje parish office said in a statement , calling on the faithful to respond “as Our Lady has been teaching us in Medjugorje for more than 40 years: with prayer, fasting, and forgiveness.” Cleanup began immediately, the parish said, and “the shrine remains open to all pilgrims.” Bishop Petar Palić of Mostar-Duvno expressed deep sorrow, urging the faithful not to let evil “infect us with its own logic,” while the Interreligious Council of Bosnia and Herzegovina condemned the attack. The Vatican granted a “nihil obstat” to devotion at Medjugorje in September 2024. Mladifest opens Aug. 1 and is expected to draw 50,000 to 60,000 pilgrims. The factory fire broke out in the early hours of Monday. Security video footage shows a masked intruder entering the perimeter just before the fire started. There was no significant damage because of the rapid response by company security personnel. This marks the latest in a cluster of unfortunate occurrences in August 2026 afflicting NATO states that seem linked to those countries’ support for Ukraine. On 7 August, Poland detained a Russian citizen in a plot to kill a person holding U.S. and Ukrainian citizenship in Warsaw. Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced the arrest on 13 August; see Report: Poland Foils Russian Hit on Ukrainian-American 'Inconvenient' to Putin – RedState . Polish prosecutors later opened a terrorism inquiry into a separate case: a fire at a WB Electronics drone plant in Skarżysko-Kamienna on 31 August. Poland has been the main target of Russian operations. In June, a Russian artist whose work criticised Putin was assassinated in Poland . Soon after, the Polish security services detained the suspected killer , who they said was using a Georgian passport. Last month, a Russian missile hit Poland during intensive attacks on Ukraine. That followed an incident last year in which around 20 Russian drones violated Polish airspace . On 13 August, a fire at a KNDS Ammo Italy factory in Colleferro was followed by a large blast. The factory makes medium- and large-caliber artillery rounds that are transferred to Ukraine. No one was killed. Italian officials said they saw no sign of a Russian link .     As an ammunition factory in Italy was accidentally blowing itself to smithereens, a major transformer fire caused a power failure that forced ExxonMobil’s Esso refinery in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, to shut down. At the same time, another refinery in Rotterdam was also hit by an explosion that killed one person and injured several others. Totally chance happenings: two refineries get shut down in the same night, in the same city, by explosions every other week. That same morning, in Rotterdam’s Botlek section, a transformer fire affected units and flare-gas systems. Separately, an explosion at Gunvor Energy’s storage terminal killed one worker and injured six. Port authorities said the outage and the Gunvor blast appeared unrelated. https://www.esmmagazine.com/retail/alime.text: Circle K parent Alimentation Couche-Tard has reported strong results in the first quarter of its 2027 fiscal year, marking its fifth consecutive quarter of same-store merchandise sales growth in the US. Adjusted EBITDA rose by 10.5%, while revenue increased by 25.1%, to $21.7 billion (€18.67 billion), compared with the first quarter of 2026, driven by acquisitions and organic growth. Total gross profit also increased by 8.7% to $3.6 billion (€3.1 billion), with operating income rising by 7.6% to $1.2 billion (€1.03 billion), over the same period. Alex Miller, president and chief executive officer of Alimentation Couche-Tard, said, “We are encouraged by the start to fiscal 2027 and the continued progress we are making through Core + More.” Quarterly Highlights Alimentation Couche-Tard highlighted that net earnings attributable to shareholders reached $828.5 million (€713.0 million) in the first quarter of 2027, up from $782.5 million (€673.3 million) in 2026. Total merchandise and service revenues also rose by 4.1% to $4.9 billion (€4.21 billion), with same-store merchandise revenues rising by 1.7% in the US, by 1.2% in Europe and other regions, while remaining relatively stable in Canada. Merchandise and service gross margin declined slightly by 0.5% in the US and by 0.6% in Canada, but increased by 0.7% in Europe and other regions. Miller added, “Our fuel business remained a source of strength, delivering solid profitability and demonstrating the resilience of our network.” Share Repurchase And Acquisition The company renewed its share repurchase programme, effective 23 July 2026, and repurchased 0.4 million shares for $26.0 million (€22.4 million) during the first quarter. Alimentation Couche-Tard also repaid its €750.0 million euro-denominated senior unsecured notes on 6 May. In addition, the company noted that it expects to receive regulatory approval for the acquisition of all outstanding shares of Polish convenience store chain Żabka Group before the end of its 2027 financial year. During the first quarter, it also acquired two company-operated stores and completed the construction of 12 stores, as well as the relocation or modernisation of 8 stores. Filipe Da Silva, chief financial officer of Alimentation Couche-Tard, commented, “[…] we continue to invest in customer value and traffic-driving initiatives, advancing our strategic priorities and focusing on delivering sustainable long-term earnings growth."

https://prague.tv/money-work/opening-a-b.text: The short version Banks normally ask for a valid passport or ID, and often a document showing your address and status in Czechia. Requirements differ between banks. Some open accounts online, while others need a branch visit. A Czech account number includes a bank code (written like 123456789/0800), and IBANs begin with CZ. On this page 9 sections What banks usually ask for Branch or online Czech account numbers EU rules and basic accounts What a Czech account does for you Fees and services The order that works Common pitfalls After you open it A Czech bank account fixes a long list of small annoyances. Landlords and employers often prefer Czech accounts, direct debits get easier, and card payments avoid foreign-transaction fees. Newcomers can usually open one, but the exact steps depend on the bank and your situation. Czech account numbers the country code that starts every Czech IBAN CZ characters in a Czech IBAN 24 Source: Czech National Bank What banks usually ask for Every bank sets its own rules, but expect to be asked for: a valid passport or other identity document (EU citizens can use a national ID card); proof of your address in Czechia, or sometimes your address abroad; evidence of your status, such as a residence permit, visa or EU registration certificate; sometimes a Czech phone number, an email address and details of your employer or income. Banks also have to follow anti-money-laundering rules, which is why the checks can feel thorough. Get your documents in order before you go and you'll save time. If a document is in neither Czech nor English, the bank may ask for a certified translation. Branch or online Some banks let you open an account entirely online, with identity checks by video call or mobile app. Others want you in a branch with your original documents. Online is easier if you've just arrived and your paperwork is complete. A branch helps if your case is unusual, since you can ask questions on the spot. Check each bank's English-language site for current requirements, and call ahead to book a branch appointment. Branch or online? Feature Branch Online Best when Your case is unusual or your documents are mixed Your paperwork is complete and standard Identity check In person with original documents Video call or app check Speed Depends on appointment availability Often quicker once documents are ready Questions Ask the adviser face to face Chat or phone support Language English staff common in central branches, not guaranteed elsewhere English app and site are common Practices differ by bank. Check each bank's English-language requirements page. Czech account numbers A Czech account number carries a bank code after a slash, for example 123456789/0800. For payments outside Czechia you use the IBAN, which starts with CZ. Domestic transfers are usually quick, and many banks offer instant payments between Czech accounts at any hour. Landlords, employers and utility companies will ask for the number with the bank code. Giving only the digits before the slash is the commonest mistake, and it makes a transfer fail or bounce. If you do not have the full number, open your banking app and copy it from the account details. EU rules and basic accounts EU rules give people legally resident in the EU a right to a basic payment account. If a bank turns you down, ask which rule it is applying, and think about trying another bank. The Czech National Bank is the regulator and publishes consumer-rights information. We don't give legal advice, so see a professional if a bank refuses without a clear reason. What a Czech account does for you The reasons to bother are practical. Rent is normally paid by standing order or bank transfer, so a Czech account makes the monthly payment automatic and removes foreign-transfer fees. Employers pay salaries into Czech accounts as a matter of routine, and utilities, mobile operators and insurers often take direct debits. A card linked to the account also works in nearly every shop and on public transport, and the bank's app gives you instant notifications and simple transfers by QR code, a payment method that is widely used in Czechia. Keep in mind that some services still ask for a Czech account before they will sign you up. That includes some landlords, some gyms and some online shops. The sooner you have one, the fewer small obstacles you meet in the first weeks. Fees and services Compare monthly account fees, card fees, ATM withdrawals at other banks and transfers abroad. Some accounts have no monthly fee if you meet conditions such as a regular deposit. Read the bank's tariff, and treat any figure in an old article with caution. Contactless cards and phone wallets are common in Prague, and most shops and public transport take them. The order that works Newcomers often face a loop: the bank wants proof of address, the landlord wants a bank account for the deposit, and the employer wants both. The loop breaks when you pick the bank with the most flexible rules for your situation, ask exactly which documents it accepts as proof of address and bring them all at once. A rental contract is the standard proof, but ask whether a letter from your employer or a registration certificate also counts. Plan the first bank visit for a quiet weekday morning, not a Friday afternoon. Staff have time to read your documents, and a missing paper can be fixed before the weekend. Common pitfalls No proof of address yet. Banks may ask for a lease or registration. If you don't have one, ask what they accept. Visa not yet issued. Some banks only accept long-term residents. Language. English-speaking staff are common in central branches but not guaranteed elsewhere. Bring a Czech speaker if you can. Changed details. If your address or permit changes, tell the bank. It may ask for new documents. From zero to a working account List two or three banks Read each one's English requirements page. Gather your documents Passport or ID, status document, proof of address and a phone number. Choose branch or online Online if your paperwork is standard, a branch if your case is unusual. Open the account and the app Set up internet banking and the mobile app straight away. Share the full number Give your employer and landlord the account number with the bank code, plus the IBAN where needed. After you open it Set up internet banking and the mobile app, give your account number to your employer and landlord, and link a card to your phone. Keep your documents handy, because banks sometimes ask to update them. Frequently asked questions Do I need Czech to open a bank account? Not necessarily. Many banks offer English-language sites and staff, especially in central branches, but it is not guaranteed everywhere. Can I open an account without a residence permit? It depends on the bank and your status. Some accept only long-term residents, so ask before you go. What is the number after the slash? The bank code. A Czech account number looks like 123456789/0800, and you need the whole thing for domestic payments. What should I do if a bank refuses me? Ask which rule it applies and try another bank. The Czech National Bank publishes consumer-rights information. Before you book an appointment, list the banks you could use, read each one's English requirements page and gather the documents. That prep is most of the process.
